Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-2-prompt-long-0030", "row_sha256": "f7889d815eac4b665ab77e246ed52675e3fd20f44f004c3988cc47da17ada0ad", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "i need a clear workshop ventilation check update for the staff and the building manager, not a formal certification report. it is for Northline Community Repair Workshop at 18 Alder Street, Bay 2. The check happened on 12 May 2025, from 8:10 to 10:05 in the morning. Mara Vale, the facilities technician, did the measurements with Joel Kim, the safety coordinator. The normal workshop was open during the check, and nobody stopped production. Please make it read like an ordinary internal update, not a regulation document or an incident report.

The monthly check covered the three extraction benches used for routine sanding and grinding in Bay 2, and the shared rooftop fan marked EF-2. EF-2 has a listed rating of 2.4 cubic metres per second. The airflow readings at the three bench branches were 2.1, 2.0 and 1.9 cubic metres per second, in that order. At the capture faces, Mara recorded 0.48, 0.51 and 0.46 metres per second. The readings were taken with a vane meter, serial VM-184, whose calibration date is 3 April 2025. Please keep the bench order clear and don't turn the readings into a pass/fail result, because no acceptance limit was included in the check notes.

There were some practical things around the room worth mentioning too. The west delivery door was opened twice for materials during the check and was shut again both times. The main personnel door stayed closed except for normal staff entry. The two high-level return grilles were visible and had no obvious blockage from the floor; no one removed them or inspected inside the duct. A strip of tissue moved toward each bench hood while the branches were running. That was only a visual observation, not a measured capture test. Joel said, “The room felt clear while we were working, but that is not a substitute for the readings.” Keep that as his comment and don't make it sound like a measured conclusion.

For the dust collector, the differential pressure gauge showed 620 pascals. The previous monthly log, dated 14 April, showed 590 pascals. The service guide lists 700 pascals as the point at which the filter should be serviced. The filter hasn't been changed during this check. A replacement filter is expected to arrive on 16 May, but it has not arrived yet. The notes say to look at the gauge again after delivery and arrange filter service if it reaches the guide's 700-pascal point. Please present that as a follow-up, not something already done. The panel was closed and the fan ran without a visible warning light during the observation period; nobody opened the electrical cabinet.

There are two pieces of equipment that need careful scope wording. The EF-1 paint-booth fan was switched off and isolated while the booth is being refurbished, so it wasn't tested and isn't covered by the readings. The welding hood also wasn't tested: stored materials blocked safe access to its capture point. A separate access check is needed before anyone measures that hood. Don't imply either piece of equipment was working or that the whole building was checked. The update should distinguish the three measured bench branches from these excluded areas.

At bench three, the damper handle felt stiff when Mara checked its position. The position mark was still visible, and she left the handle where it was. No adjustment or repair was made. Maintenance should arrange lubrication during a planned downtime slot and confirm that the handle moves freely afterward; there isn't a date for that work yet. Please don't say the damper has been repaired or that the branch was rebalanced. The other two handles moved normally during the visual check. No unusual noise was noted from EF-2, though the check did not include vibration testing.

The room's portable monitor logged carbon dioxide only. There is no particulate reading in this month's log, and the check did not include personal exposure sampling, a smoke test, or a review of regulatory compliance. The update can say these items weren't part of the check, but it shouldn't suggest that missing tests found a problem or proved that there is no problem. Keep the report limited to what Mara and Joel observed, what the listed instruments showed, and the follow-up items above. The ventilation check is a routine monthly one, not a wider assessment of the refurbishment or workshop operations.

Could you organize the update with a short opening that identifies the date, people and purpose, then a numbered section for the measured benches and equipment, followed by practical observations and follow-up actions? Include Joel's quoted comment in the observations. End with a separate final paragraph that carries the full assessment and its conditions: the notes support an assessment of ventilation as adequate for routine bench work only in the inspected zones while the extraction serving benches one through three is running; they do not support an assessment of the paint booth, the welding hood, or other work conditions. Keep the limitation about the missing particulate data and the untested areas alongside that final assessment. Don't add a recommendation that everyone resume work, an approval, or a broader conclusion.", "output": "Write an ordinary internal ventilation-check update for the staff and building manager at Northline Community Repair Workshop, 18 Alder Street, Bay 2. This is a routine monthly check, not a formal certification report, incident report, or wider assessment of refurbishment or workshop operations.

The check took place on 12 May 2025, from 8:10 to 10:05 a.m. Facilities technician Mara Vale took the measurements with safety coordinator Joel Kim. The workshop remained open and production was not stopped.

1. Measured benches and equipment

The check covered the three extraction benches used for routine sanding and grinding in Bay 2 and their shared rooftop fan, EF-2, rated at 2.4 cubic metres per second. In bench order, branch airflow readings were 2.1, 2.0 and 1.9 cubic metres per second. Capture-face readings were 0.48, 0.51 and 0.46 metres per second, respectively. Mara used vane meter VM-184, calibrated on 3 April 2025. No acceptance limit was included in the check notes, so report the readings without assigning a pass/fail result.

The dust collector’s differential pressure gauge read 620 pascals; the previous monthly log, dated 14 April, read 590 pascals. The service guide identifies 700 pascals as the filter-service point. The filter was not changed during this check. A replacement is expected on 16 May but has not arrived. Record a follow-up to recheck the gauge after delivery and arrange filter service if the reading reaches 700 pascals. The panel was closed, and no visible warning light appeared while the fan was observed running. The electrical cabinet was not opened.

2. Observations and scope

The west delivery door was opened twice for materials and shut both times. The main personnel door remained closed apart from normal staff entry. From the floor, the two high-level return grilles appeared unobstructed; they were not removed, and the inside of the duct was not inspected. While the branches were running, a strip of tissue moved toward each bench hood. Describe this as a visual observation, not a measured capture test. Include Joel’s comment exactly: “The room felt clear while we were working, but that is not a substitute for the readings.” Make clear that it is his comment, not a measured conclusion.

The EF-1 paint-booth fan was switched off and isolated while the booth is being refurbished. It was not tested and is outside the readings. The welding hood was also not tested because stored materials blocked safe access to its capture point; a separate access check is needed before it can be measured. Distinguish these excluded areas from the three measured bench branches. Do not imply that the paint booth or welding hood was working, or that the whole building was checked.

At bench three, Mara found the damper handle stiff. Its position mark was visible, and she left it where it was; no adjustment or repair was made. Maintenance should arrange lubrication during a planned downtime slot and confirm afterward that the handle moves freely. No date has been set. Do not describe the damper as repaired or the branch as rebalanced. The other two handles moved normally during the visual check. No unusual noise was noted from EF-2, but vibration testing was not included.

The portable room monitor logged carbon dioxide only. This month’s log contains no particulate reading. The check also did not include personal exposure sampling, a smoke test, or a regulatory-compliance review. State these limits without implying that missing tests found a problem or proved there is no problem. Keep the update restricted to the observations, instrument readings and follow-up items recorded above.

End with a separate final paragraph preserving this complete, conditional assessment: the notes support an assessment of ventilation as adequate for routine bench work only in the inspected zones while the extraction serving benches one through three is running. They do not support an assessment of the paint booth, welding hood or other work conditions. Keep the missing particulate data and untested areas as limitations alongside that assessment. Do not add a recommendation that everyone resume work, an approval, or a broader conclusion."}]
